name: judy
desc: State-of-the-art C library that implements a sparse dynamic array
why: A sparse dynamic array library with a clever trie-based design; an unusual data structure worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: Judy is a C library that implements a sparse dynamic array. Per the homepage, Judy arrays are declared with a null pointer and consume memory only when populated, yet can grow to use available memory. The API uses simple insert, retrieve, and delete calls, and sort, search, count, and sequential access are built in. The page says Judy can replace arrays, sparse arrays, hash tables, B-trees, binary trees, linear lists, skiplists, and some sort and search and counting code. The homepage does not describe the inputs and outputs in detail.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents Judy as a scalable, high-performance, memory-efficient way to get dynamically sized and associative arrays without rework for expansion or contraction. It says tuning and configuring are not required, and in fact not even possible.
brief.standout: The homepage claims a single structure can stand in for many common data structures (hash tables, B-trees, skiplists, and others) while needing no tuning. It also says the array is unbounded, sized only by machine memory, and allocates only for populated elements. The scout note calls the design trie-based, but the homepage I read does not confirm that.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage footer reads 'Modified: 11/10/04' and '© 2004 Judy Team', so the site has not been updated in a long time. I did not check the Downloads or News pages for a later release, and brew provided no version info.
brief.caveats: The homepage is short and marketing-toned, with no code sample, platform list, or license on this page. Its only technical content is in linked pages (a 10-minute and a 3-hour technical description, Documentation, Downloads, Errors, Glossary) that I did not follow, because the fetch returned text with the link URLs stripped. The 'state-of-the-art' wording is the project's own phrasing from 2004. The homepage was reachable.
quotes: Judy arrays are declared simply with a null pointer.
A Judy array consumes memory only when it is populated, yet can grow to take advantage of all available memory if desired.
Tuning and configuring are not required (in fact not even possible).
